# 1 Maccabees Chapter 13 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 13 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 13 marks the pivot of the book: Jonathan's death, Simon's assumption of leadership, and culminating in v.41 — "the yoke of the Gentiles was lifted from Israel" — the formal declaration of Hasmonean independence (142 BCE). This verse and v.42's new dating formula are among the most theologically and historically significant in the entire work.

**Key term rulings:**
- "yoke of the Gentiles" (v.41) — rendered literally; the phrase echoes Jer 28:11, Nah 1:13; must not be weakened
- "the great high priest, commander, and leader of the Jews" (v.42) — the full title preserved; "leader" for ἡγούμενος
- "Friend of Kings" (v.36) — capitalized court title (plural: multiple kings have honored Simon)
- "palm branches" (v.51) — preserved; a liturgical detail
- Monument description (vv.27-29) — the architectural and symbolic details preserved closely
- "to this day" (v.30) — preserved; standard authorial timestamp
- Simon's speech (vv.3-6) — close to EMET register; formal oratory deserving dignity

---

**1** When Simon heard that Trypho had assembled a large army to come into the land of Judea and destroy it,

**2** and saw that the people were trembling with fear, he went up to Jerusalem and gathered the people together.

**3** He encouraged them and said: "You yourselves know all that my brothers and I and my father's house have done for the sake of the laws and the sanctuary — the wars and the hardships we have seen.

**4** For this reason all my brothers have perished for Israel's sake, and I alone am left.

**5** Far be it from me to spare my own life in any time of tribulation, for I am not better than my brothers.

**6** Rather I will avenge my nation and the sanctuary and your wives and children, for all the nations have gathered to destroy us out of pure hatred."

**7** The spirit of the people was rekindled when they heard these words.

**8** They answered with a great voice: "You are our leader in place of Judas and Jonathan your brothers.

**9** Fight our battles; and all that you tell us, we will do."

**10** He mustered all the fighting men and hastened to finish the walls of Jerusalem and to fortify it all around.

**11** He sent Jonathan son of Absalom with a considerable force to Joppa; Jonathan expelled the inhabitants and remained in it.

**12** Trypho set out to invade the land with a large army and encamped at Adora; Simon and his army kept pace with him wherever he turned.

**13** Trypho encamped against Baskama.

**14** When Trypho saw that Simon had taken his brother Jonathan's place, he sent word to Simon:

**15** "We are holding your brother Jonathan on account of the hundred talents of silver he owed to the royal treasury for the offices he held, and because of the two sons whom he left with us as hostages.

**16** Send a hundred talents of silver and his two sons, and we will release him; otherwise we will not release him."

**17** Simon knew that they spoke to him with deceit, yet he ordered the money and the boys to be sent, lest he incur great hostility among the people,

**18** who might say: "It was because he did not send the money and the boys that Jonathan perished."

**19** He sent the boys and the hundred talents — and Trypho deceived him and did not release Jonathan.

**20** After this Trypho came to invade and ravage the country, going around by the road through Adora; Simon and his army shadowed him at every turn.

**21** The men in the citadel sent to Trypho urging him to come through the wilderness and to send them provisions.

**22** Trypho prepared all his cavalry to advance, but that night there fell a very heavy snowfall, and he could not advance because of the snow; he therefore withdrew and went into Gilead.

**23** When he came near Baskama, he killed Jonathan, who was buried there.

**24** Then Trypho turned back and returned to his own land.

**25** Simon sent and recovered the bones of Jonathan his brother and buried him at Modein, the city of his ancestors.

**26** All Israel made great lamentation for him and mourned him for many days.

**27** Simon built a monument over the tomb of his father and his brothers, raising it high with polished stone, both front and back.

**28** He set up seven pyramids facing one another, for his father, his mother, and his four brothers.

**29** Around the pyramids he erected great columns, and on the columns he placed suits of armor as an everlasting memorial; beside the armor he carved ships, so that they could be seen by all who sail the sea.

**30** This is the tomb he made at Modein, and it stands to this day.

**31** Trypho dealt treacherously with the young King Antiochus and killed him,

**32** and became king in his place, put on the crown of Asia, and brought great disaster on the land.

**33** Simon rebuilt the strongholds of Judea, fortifying them with high towers and great walls, with gates and bars, and he laid up provisions in the strongholds.

**34** Simon also chose envoys and sent them to King Demetrius requesting that he grant the country relief, since all that Trypho was doing was plundering it.

**35** King Demetrius replied to him with this letter:

**36** "King Demetrius to Simon the high priest and Friend of Kings, and to the elders and to the Jewish nation, greetings.

**37** The golden crown and the palm branch that you sent, we have received; and we are prepared to make a full peace with you and to write to the royal officials to grant you remissions.

**38** Whatever we have confirmed to you remains confirmed; and the strongholds that you have built shall be yours.

**39** We pardon all offenses and faults committed up to this day, and remit the crown tax that you owe; and whatever other levy was formerly collected in Jerusalem shall be collected no more.

**40** Any among you who are qualified for service in our forces, let them be enrolled; and let there be peace between us."

**41** In the one hundred and seventieth year the yoke of the Gentiles was lifted from Israel,

**42** and the people began to write in their documents and contracts: "In the first year of Simon, the great high priest, commander, and leader of the Jews."

**43** In those days Simon encamped against Gazara and surrounded it with his troops; he constructed a siege engine, brought it against the city, struck a tower, and captured it.

**44** The men in the engine leaped down into the city, and a great tumult broke out in the city.

**45** The men of the city went up on the wall with their wives and children, tore their clothes, and cried out in a great voice, pleading with Simon to give them his right hand;

**46** they said: "Do not treat us according to our wickedness but according to your mercy."

**47** Simon was reconciled to them and stopped fighting against them. He expelled them from the city and purified the houses in which the idols had been, then entered it with hymns and blessings.

**48** He removed all uncleanness from it, settled in it men who observed the law, and strengthened it, making his own residence there.

**49** Those in the citadel in Jerusalem were prevented from going out to the countryside, or from buying and selling; they were in great want, and many of them died of famine.

**50** They cried out to Simon to accept their surrender, and he gave them his right hand. He expelled them from the citadel and cleansed it from its pollutions.

**51** He entered it on the twenty-third day of the second month, in the one hundred and seventy-first year, with praise and waving of palm branches, and with harps, cymbals, and lutes, with hymns and songs, because a great enemy had been trampled down out of Israel.

**52** He ordained that this day should be observed every year with joy and gladness. He strengthened the hill of the temple that stood beside the citadel, and he and his companions dwelt there.

**53** Simon saw that his son John had grown to manhood, and he made him commander of all the forces; and John dwelt at Gazara.
